newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end up, offsetting losses on Tokyo stock fall.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end up, offsetting losses on Tokyo stock fall.

text.p: The cash and futures JGBs ended firmer on Friday, particularly in the shorter-end of the market, more than offsetting early losses incurred by the Tokyo stock market tumble, traders said.
In late trade, the JGBs shook off the early depression with some 'flight-to-quality' buying which benefitted the shorter-end of the yield curve most, traders said.
Earlier, the JGBs fell substantially for fear that financial institutions may be forced to sell JGBs and take profits to offset steep losses on Tokyo stocks, they said.
Key March JGB ended at 125.05, up from 124.89 on Thursday.
The Nikkei average of 225 leading shares fell more than 500 points, or 2.5 percent, the first time it had fallen below the key level of 20,000 in three months.
It recovered some ground and ended at 20,341.39.

"Too much losses on stocks usually induce profit-taking on JGBs, but somewhat milder losses lead to flight-to-quality buying in the fixed income sector as was the case of today," said a European bank trader.
The key September Euroyen contract was up sharply at 99.24, compared with 99.17 on Thursday.
The yield of the 182nd 10-year JGB was at 2.460 percent, down from 2.470 percent close on Thursday.
Meanwhile, the Tokyo stock tumble prompted another phenomenon in the interbank market.
The Japan premium -- the extra cost Japanese banks are charged when raising funds in the Euro interbank market -- rose on Friday due to the steep losses on the Tokyo stock market.
Major Japanese city banks with comparatively good ratings paid a premium of 25 basis points (BPS) over the prevailing one-month Eurodollar deposit rate of 5.53125 percent.
This compared with a premium of 17 BPS a week ago.

Some traders said that the recent significant weakness in Japanese bank shares induced speculation, though not widespread, in the market that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) may move to lower the current ceiling of the key overnight call rate to around 0.45 percent from the current 0.50 percent.

In the next few weeks, the market is anticipating a cash flow into JGBs from the government's scheme to wind up failed mortgage firms, traders said. Under the government's scheme, agricultural financial institutions are expected to receive some 2.7 trillion yen later this month.
